focus: The action between two screens, and prose that already holds the answer
answeredQuestions: How should the action that moves between two screens be found, and what happens when it is only implied?
How should prose rules and acceptance criteria become decisions and branches without inventing either?

label: An acceptance criterion is already a labelled edge (Given state, When action, Then outcome, one outcome per line) and the packet flattens the one pre-structured input type into prose
A criterion deliberately omits the mechanism, so a Then with no When is a named gap and an Epic's release-level criterion names no screen and contributes no node

The house already carries an unknown value as an Open line or TBD rather than an inferred estimate, while Flow Mode requires the source's own words and sends anything missing to Left out, so the two packets disagree about an open value on a label

The provenance table classifies a node and only adds an edge row when the source differs from its ends, so an inferred user-flow connector carries no source class at all, coarser than the per-claim classification the intake claims to apply

A contradicted edge becomes a finding with no surface: the gate ends at one question, the rubric removes the connector and reports nothing, so the most important conflict leaves no node, no row and no Left out line
No public source in the corpus gives support-ticket to diagram guidance, and Doc Mode's scope limit implies a ticket proves an error path exists but never the trigger that reaches it

direction: Read a support ticket as a source of the trigger that reaches the error it reports
reason: No corpus source supports it, and Doc Mode limits an authority signal to the scope it covers, so a ticket evidences the exit state only
